THE FRAMEWORK IS NOT A COMBATANT. The framework is the Rules of Engagement and Rules of Interaction -- Isaiah 28:10 method, the L1-L4 layer rules, the burden rule -- and it binds BOTH combatants equally. The debate is about the TOPIC. The DEFENDER holds a chain of interlocking citations on the topic; the CHALLENGER presses an opposing view and settles it only by breaking that chain. A claim by either side that restates resolved ground with its stating verses cited is not an overpress.
This debate was CHAIN-SCOPED (Isaiah 28:10 declared): judge whether the DEFENDER'S CHAIN on the topic survived as a chain -- isolated-link objections that never engage the chain do not break it. The rule cuts both ways: an objection that is itself a floating [L4] (no exhibited layer footing) cannot break a link that exhibits its footing. Name every floating [L4] on either side before weighing it; an [L4] floats only when the block that states it exhibits fewer than two prior layers ([L1]-[L3]) for it; that one test applies to the defender and the challenger alike. That no quoted row states an [L4] is never a reason to call it floating: an [L4] is an inference by definition, and that demand is the retired stating-verse test, at a collision as everywhere else. The same holds against the challenger: a challenger premise or answer whose support is that no verse states the defender's link, or an exclusion, in its own words is that retired test and is not SUPPORTED on that ground. A reading cited from the Septuagint (LXX) is a citation error for either side: name it at the citation check and give it no weight as footing. A judge that names an [L4] floating names, in the same sentence, the layers its block exhibits and the layer it lacks. An [L4] whose block exhibits two or more prior layers is footed for either side and is weighed at its collision on the rows it rests on; the witnesses held to contradict it are quoted, and they contradict it read together, line upon line; an inference admitted through the prior layers (Isaiah 28:10) is EVIDENCE, an inference that floats free of the text is not.

TOPIC: Did Christ have a biological father?
=== [CR1] DEFENDER R1 ===
DEFENDER (standard reading) -- ROUND 1, OPENING

# Opening: Christ had no biological human father

**Position.** The KJV says Jesus was conceived in Mary by the Holy Ghost, without any man. Joseph was his husband-of-record and protector, not his begetter. The case is one interlocking chain, not a single proof-text.

## I. The genealogy breaks its own pattern (Matthew 1:16)

**[L1]** Matthew 1:2-15 runs unbroken: "Abraham begat Isaac; and Isaac begat Jacob…" Then verse 16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, **of whom was born Jesus**, who is called Christ."

**[L2]** The verb "begat" is *egennēsen* (he fathered), active, with a man as subject. It is used for every father in the list. At the last step Matthew changes the verb to *egennēthē* (was born), which is passive. He also changes the subject. The relative pronoun *hēs* (of whom) is **feminine singular**, so it can refer only to Mary. It cannot be "of whom" in the masculine, and it cannot be plural, "of whom both."

**[L4]** The footing is Matthew 1:2-16 (the fixed "begat" pattern) and the Greek feminine singular *hēs*. The chain: an author who has said "begat" forty times and then switches verb, voice and gender at the one point where the line reaches Jesus has deliberately withheld the father's role from Joseph. Joseph is "the husband of Mary," not the one who "begat."

**[L3]** Luke 3:23 matches this. Jesus began to be about thirty, "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph." *Enomizeto* means "was reckoned or thought by custom." Luke marks the sonship as reputed, not real.

## II. The conception was "of the Holy Ghost," before any union (Matthew 1:18-20; Luke 1:34-35)

**[L1]** Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, **before they came together**, she was found with child **of the Holy Ghost**." Matthew 1:20: "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."

**[L2]** *Ek pneumatos hagiou* means "out of the Holy Spirit," and *ek* marks source or origin. *Gennēthen* (that which is begotten or conceived) is neuter and passive. The agent is not named as Joseph. *Prin ē synelthein autous* means "before they came together," so the pregnancy is dated before any union.

**[L1]** Luke 1:34: "How shall this be, **seeing I know not a man**?" Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: **therefore also** that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."

**[L2]** *Andra ou ginōskō* (I know not a man) uses the present tense for her ongoing state. *Episkiasei* means "will overshadow." *Dio kai* means "for which reason also," so the cause of the title is the conception described just before it.

**[L4]** The footing is Matthew 1:18-20 (*ek*, source, and *prin*, timing) and Luke 1:34-35 (Mary's *ou ginōskō* and the angel's *dio kai*). The chain: Mary's question excludes any man as the means, and the angel's answer supplies a non-human source in place of one. The conception therefore has no male human contribution.

## III. The sign: a virgin (Isaiah 7:14; Matthew 1:22-23)

**[L1]** Matthew 1:22-23: "that it might be fulfilled which was spoken of the Lord by the prophet, saying, Behold, **a virgin** shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son."

**[L2]** The Hebrew in Isaiah 7:14 is *ʿalmāh* (a young woman of marriageable age, unmarried). The Greek Matthew uses is *parthenos* (virgin). Matthew's inspired rendering fixes the sense.

**[L3]** Genesis 24:43 uses *ʿalmāh* of Rebekah. Genesis 24:16 describes the same woman as "a virgin, neither had any man known her." The word is therefore used in the text for an unmarried virgin. Isaiah 7:14 calls the birth a "sign" (*ʾôt*), and an ordinary conception within marriage would be no sign.

**[L4]** The footing is Matthew 1:22-23 (*parthenos*) and Genesis 24:16, 43 (*ʿalmāh* applied to a virgin). The chain: the sign promised in Isaiah is the one Matthew says was fulfilled. A virgin who conceived did so without a man.

## IV. Joseph was husband and legal father, not begetter (Matthew 1:25; Luke 2:48-49)

**[L1]** Matthew 1:25: Joseph "**knew her not till** she had brought forth her firstborn son: and he called his name JESUS."

**[L2]** *Ouk eginōsken … heōs hou* means "he was not knowing her until which time," an imperfect tense for continued abstention through the whole pregnancy.

**[L1]** Luke 2:48: "Thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing." Luke 2:49: "wist ye not that I must be about **my Father's** business?"

**[L4]** The footing is Matthew 1:25 (*ouk eginōsken*, continued abstention through the pregnancy) and Luke 2:48-49. The chain: Mary's "thy father" is the household's usage, and Jesus answers in the very next verse by naming a different Father. The text sets the two usages side by side and corrects the first with the second. The same pattern appears in Luke 3:23 ("as was supposed") and John 6:42, where the crowd says "the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know." John 6:42 records the crowd's words and does not assert them as true.

## V. Davidic descent does not need Joseph's seed

**[L1]** Romans 1:3: "made of the seed of David according to the flesh." Acts 2:30: God swore "that of the fruit of his loins, **according to the flesh**, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne." Galatians 4:4: "God sent forth his Son, **made of a woman**."

**[L2]** *Genomenou ek spermatos Dauid kata sarka* means "having come into being out of the seed of David according to flesh." Galatians 4:4 says *genomenon ek gynaikos*, "come into being out of a woman," and names no man.

**[L3]** Jeremiah 22:30 says of Jeconiah, "no man of his seed shall prosper, sitting upon the throne of David." Matthew 1:11-12 places Jechonias in Joseph's line. Genesis 3:15 speaks of "her seed" (*zeraʿ*, seed), which is unusual because seed is normally reckoned to the man.

**[L4]** The footing is Romans 1:3 and Acts 2:30 (Jesus is of David "according to the flesh") and Jeremiah 22:30 with Matthew 1:11-12 (Joseph's line carried a bar on the throne). The chain: the flesh-descent from David runs through Mary, who is the only human parent the text names for his body. Joseph's line gives legal title through adoption and naming (Matthew 1:21, 25). This avoids Jeconiah's bar, which a begotten son of Joseph would have inherited.

## DECLARED CHAIN -- the links your case stands on:

1. Matthew 1:16 changes verb, voice and gender (*egennēsen* to *egennēthē*; feminine singular *hēs*), so the line of begetting stops at Joseph and the birth is "of" Mary alone. Footing: [L1] Matthew 1:2-16; [L2] *hēs* (of whom, feminine) and *egennēthē* (was born); [L3] Luke 3:23 "as was supposed."
2. The conception was "of the Holy Ghost" before any union, and Mary says she knows no man. Footing: [L1] Matthew 1:18-20, Luke 1:34-35; [L2] *ek pneumatos hagiou* (out of the Holy Spirit), *prin synelthein* (before coming together), *dio kai* (for which reason also).
3. The sign is a virgin conceiving, with *parthenos* fixing the sense of *ʿalmāh*. Footing: [L1] Matthew 1:22-23; [L2] *ʿalmāh* (young woman) and *parthenos* (virgin); [L3] Genesis 24:43 with 24:16.
4. Joseph is husband and reputed father only, and Jesus himself names a different Father. Footing: [L1] Matthew 1:25, Luke 2:48-49, Luke 3:23; [L2] *ouk eginōsken* (was not knowing her) and *enomizeto* (was reckoned); [L3] John 6:42 as the crowd's words.
5. Davidic descent "according to the flesh" runs through Mary, and Joseph's line carried Jeconiah's bar. Footing: [L1] Romans 1:3, Acts 2:30, Galatians 4:4; [L2] *ek gynaikos* (out of a woman) and *kata sarka* (according to flesh); [L3] Jeremiah 22:30 with Matthew 1:11-12.
6. Christ had no biological human father: he was conceived in Mary by the Holy Ghost, and Joseph was husband and legal father only. Footing: links 1-5, resting on [L1] Matthew 1:16-25 and Luke 1:34-35, [L2] *hēs*, *ek pneumatos hagiou* and *ou ginōskō* (I know not), and [L3] Isaiah 7:14 with Genesis 24:16, 43.
=== [DR1] CHALLENGER R1 ===
CHALLENGER (record's reading) -- ROUND 1, CHALLENGE

# CHALLENGER'S REPLY — "of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh"

The keystone **LINK 6** ("Christ had no biological human father") is answered by the defense's own verses, so I start there and work down.

## 1. LINK 5 and LINK 6 — the flesh rows name a man's loins, and the only Davidic man the birth chapters name is Joseph

[L1] Acts 2:30: "Therefore being a prophet, and knowing that God had sworn with an oath to him, that **of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh**, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne." Romans 1:3: "Concerning his Son Jesus Christ our Lord, which was **made of the seed of David according to the flesh**."

[L1] The oath itself: 2 Samuel 7:12 "I will set up thy seed after thee, **which shall proceed out of thy bowels**"; Psalm 132:11 "Of **the fruit of thy body** will I set upon thy throne"; Genesis 35:11 "kings shall come **out of thy loins**"; 1 Kings 8:19 "thy son that shall come forth **out of thy loins**."

[L2] "Loins" at Acts 2:30 is *osphys*, the same loins-word used of Levi standing "in the loins of his father" (Hebrews 7:9-10); "bowels" at 2 Samuel 7:12 is *mimme'eykha* (out of thy bowels). These are body-words of a man.

[L1] The man the text names: Luke 1:27 "espoused to a man whose name was **Joseph, of the house of David**; and the virgin's name was Mary." Luke 2:4 "Joseph also went up... (because **he was of the house and lineage of David**:)". The angel: "Joseph, **thou son of David**" (Matthew 1:20).

[L4] **Footing = [L1] Acts 2:30, Romans 1:3, 2 Samuel 7:12, Psalm 132:11, Luke 1:27, Luke 2:4 + [L2] *osphys*, *mimme'eykha*.** Link: "of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh" is a seed-row out of a man's body; the text names exactly one man of the house of David in the birth chapters, Joseph. D5's answer — "the flesh-descent from David runs through Mary" — is the move the text does not make.

## 2. Against LINK 5's "through Mary": no row states Mary's descent, and the reckoning is by the father's house

[L1] The only kin row the text gives Mary is Luke 1:36 "thy cousin Elisabeth," and Elisabeth's line is Luke 1:5 "his wife was **of the daughters of Aaron**." No Davidic name is attached to Mary anywhere in the canon.

[L1] The reckoning rule: Numbers 1:2 "after their families, **by the house of their fathers**"; 1:18 "they declared their pedigrees... **by the house of their fathers**." Ezra 2:61-62: priests who "took a wife of the daughters of Barzillai... and **was called after their name**... sought their register among those that were reckoned by genealogy, but they were not found: therefore were they, **as polluted, put from the priesthood**."

[L1] Hebrews 7:14: "For **it is evident** that our Lord sprang out of Juda..."

[L4] **Footing = [L1] Numbers 1:2, 18; Ezra 2:61-62; Hebrews 7:14; Luke 1:5, 36 + [L2] *beth 'av* (father's house).** Link: a wife's-house route is the route the register excludes in the text's own example; "evident" sprouting out of Judah therefore requires a named line — and the named line is Joseph's. **Question to the defender: how is it "evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda," given Numbers 1:2, 18, if the flesh runs through a woman whose house the text never names?**

Three more of D5's props fall at the row level:

[L1/L3] "her seed" (Genesis 3:15) never excludes a father: the same idiom is said of Hagar (Genesis 16:10 "I will multiply thy seed exceedingly") and of Rebekah (Genesis 24:60 "be thou the mother of thousands of millions"), and both bear seed with a named father (Genesis 16:15-16 "Hagar bare **Ishmael to Abram**"; Genesis 25:21 "Rebekah conceived" of Isaac). [L4, footing L1+L3]: the idiom is an offspring idiom, not a no-father idiom.

[L1/L3] Galatians 4:4 "made of a woman" is the mortality idiom: Job 25:4 "how can he be clean **that is born of a woman**?"; Matthew 11:11 "Among them that are **born of women** there hath not risen a greater than John the Baptist" — and John's father is named (Luke 1:13 "thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son"; Luke 1:63 "His name is John"). [L4, footing L1+L3]: "of a woman" never means "without a father" at any row.

[L1] The Jeconiah bar is never applied to Jesus' throne by any row: Jeremiah 22:30 "no man of his seed shall prosper, sitting upon the throne of David," yet 1 Chronicles 3:17-18 names his sons, Matthew 1:12 says "Jechonias begat Salathiel," and the plucked signet (22:24) is set on "Zerubbabel... the son of Shealtiel" (Haggai 2:23) who was **governor** (Haggai 1:1; Ezra 3:2), never king. Jeremiah's own rule stands: 18:7-8 "If that nation... turn from their evil, **I will repent of the evil**." Luke 3:27 gives Salathiel "of Neri," and the text never says whether it is the same man. [L4, footing L1+L3]: the bar is a bridge the defense supplies; it cannot route flesh through a line the text never states.

## 3. LINK 2 — the timing rows date a finding and bound an abstinence; "of the Holy Ghost" is the covenant-origin marker

[L1] Matthew 1:18: "before they came together, **she was found with child**" — the sentence dates what was *found*. [L2] *synelthein* (to come together) names married union ("come together again," 1 Corinthians 7:5); Matthew names the coming together at 1:24, "**took unto him his wife**." [L1] 1:25 "knew her not **till** she had brought forth her firstborn son: and **he called his name JESUS**" — "till" bounds the abstinence to the pregnancy.

[L2] Luke 1:34 *andra ou ginōskō* is **present active indicative** — "I know not a man," her state when the angel spoke, not a vow.

[L2/L3] *ek pneumatos hagiou* (out of the Holy Ghost) is the covenant-origin pattern, never biological paternity: John 1:13 "born of God"; 1 John 3:9; 5:1 "born of God"; 1 John 4:7 "is of God." When the canon marks biological origin it says *kata sarka* — "according to the flesh" (Romans 1:3). [L2/L3] The angel's own verbs: "the Holy Ghost shall **come upon** thee" (*eperchomai*) is Acts 1:8 "after that the Holy Ghost is **come upon** you," said of the apostles; "shall **overshadow** thee" (*episkiazō*) is the transfiguration cloud (Luke 9:34) and Peter's shadow (Acts 5:15) — presence and power at every row, begetting at none.

[L1] The canon's stated means of begetting: Genesis 4:1 "And Adam **knew** Eve his wife: and she conceived, and bare Cain." [L1/L3] The two were husband and wife in law from the espousal: "Joseph her husband" (Matthew 1:19), "Mary thy wife" (1:20), and Deuteronomy 22:24 calls a betrothed damsel "**his neighbour's wife**."

[L4] **Footing = [L1] Matthew 1:18, 25; Genesis 4:1; Matthew 1:19-20 + [L3] Deuteronomy 22:24; 1 Corinthians 7:5.** Link: the rows hold that **Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal**, and the child is of his loins. That is the sentence the seed rows require and the timing rows permit.

## 4. LINK 4 and LINK 1 — the father is named in five registers; the two "fathers" are two registers, not a denial

[L1] Mary's mouth: Luke 2:48 "behold, **thy father and I** have sought thee sorrowing." The narrator: Luke 2:27 "**the parents** brought in the child Jesus"; 2:41 "**his parents** went to Jerusalem"; 2:33 "Joseph and his mother marvelled." The town: Luke 4:22 "Is not this **the son of Joseph**?"; John 6:42 "the son of Joseph, **whose father and mother we know**." A disciple: John 1:45 "Jesus of Nazareth, **the son of Joseph**." The angel: Matthew 1:20 "Joseph, thou son of David."

[L1/L3] Luke 2:49 "my Father's business" is the covenant register, which the canon keeps beside the begetting register in one verse: 1 Chronicles 28:6 "Solomon **thy son**, he shall build my house... for **I have chosen him to be my son**, and I will be his father." Acts 13:33 applies "this day have I begotten thee" to **the resurrection**; Romans 1:4 "declared to be the Son of God... **by the resurrection**"; and Luke 1:32 gives the title with the throne **before** Mary's question at 1:34.

[L4] **Footing = [L1] Luke 2:48-49; 1 Chronicles 28:6; Acts 13:33 + [L3] 2 Samuel 7:14; Luke 1:32-34.** Link: the covenant title never deletes the father who begat — Solomon is "thy son" to David and "my son" to God in one breath. So "my Father" (Luke 2:49) does not correct "thy father" (2:48); it speaks in the other register.

[L1] Matthew 1:16 is a **birth** clause: "of whom was **born** Jesus, who is called Christ." [L2] *egennēthē* is passive — non-narration of a begetting is not a denial of one. The same chapter gives the father-act to Joseph: "thou shalt call his name JESUS" (1:21) and "he called his name JESUS" (1:25) — and the canon gives the naming to the father (Luke 1:13 to Zacharias; 1:62-63 "they made signs to **his father**, how he would have him called"). [L1/L2] Luke 3:23 immediately runs the line "which was the son of Heli" **through Joseph**, and *enomizeto* ("was supposed") is the same verb form as Acts 16:13 "where prayer **was wont** to be made" — a usage-word carrying no verdict of its own.

[L4] **Footing = [L1] Matthew 1:16, 21, 25; Luke 1:13, 62-63; 3:23 + [L2] *egennēthē*, *enomizeto*.** Link: a passive verb cannot do the work D1 assigns it ("deliberately withheld the father's role") when the same chapter has Joseph perform the father's naming, and the next chapter of Luke runs David's line through him.

## 5. LINK 3 — the sign is bounded in its own chapter

[L1] Isaiah 7:11 "Ask thee a sign"; 7:14 "the Lord himself shall give **you** a sign" (1611 margin "or, thou, O virgin, shalt call"); 7:16 "For **before the child shall know to refuse the evil, and choose the good**, the land that thou abhorrest shall be forsaken of both her kings."; 8:3-4 the prophetess bears the child; 8:8 "O Immanuel."

[L2] The word at 7:14 is *ha-almah* (the young woman); the virgin-word *bethulah* is what the defender's own pair uses at Genesis 24:16 "a virgin, neither had any man known her" — and 24:43 calls the same woman *almah*. Both words describe Rebekah.

[L4] **Footing = [L1] Isaiah 7:11, 16; 8:3-4, 8 + [L2] *almah*, *bethulah*.** Link: the sign in its own chapter is bounded to a child in Isaiah's day and recurs by name at 8:8 there; the sign therefore cannot carry the mechanism D6 asserts. Matthew 1:23's "a virgin" stands as written, and it says nothing of seed, loins, or a father.

---

## UNSUPPORTED [L4] PREMISES (the defender's words, quoted verbatim)

1. **D5:** "The flesh-descent from David runs through Mary, who is the only human parent the text names for his body." — No exhibited footing: no row states Mary's Davidic descent; the one kin row names a wife "of the daughters of Aaron" (Luke 1:5, 36).
2. **D5:** "This avoids Jeconiah's bar, which a begotten son of Joseph would have inherited." — Inference with no row applying the bar to Jesus; 1 Chronicles 3:17-18, Haggai 2:23 and Jeremiah 18:7-8 are unmet.
3. **D2:** "The conception therefore has no male human contribution." — Contradicted by Acts 2:30 "of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh," 2 Samuel 7:12 "out of thy bowels," and the stated means, Genesis 4:1.
4. **D3:** "A virgin who conceived did so without a man." — Rests on the sign while the sign's own bounds (Isaiah 7:16; 8:3-4, 8) go unexhibited.
5. **D1:** "has deliberately withheld the father's role from Joseph." — Intent-inference from a passive birth-verb, while Matthew 1:21, 25 has Joseph name the child.
6. **D4:** "Mary's 'thy father' is the household's usage." — Unfooted; and Luke 2:27's narrator's "the parents" is not answered at all.

---

**The case, in one line each:** [L1] the seed is "of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh" (Acts 2:30; Romans 1:3) — a man's body; [L1] the father is named in five registers (Luke 2:48, 2:27, 4:22, John 1:45, 6:42, Matthew 1:20); [L1] the reckoning is "by the house of their fathers" (Numbers 1:2, 18) and Joseph is "of the house and lineage of David" (Luke 2:4); [L1] the stated means is "Adam knew Eve his wife: and she conceived" (Genesis 4:1), and they were "husband" and "wife" (Matthew 1:19-20) with "till" bounding the abstinence to the pregnancy (1:25). [L4, footing L1 + L3 as above]: **Christ had a biological father — Joseph, the named Davidic father.**

**And the question stands:** By what reckoning is it "evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda" (Hebrews 7:14), given Numbers 1:2, 18 — if the flesh runs through a house the text never names?
=== [CR2] DEFENDER R2 ===
DEFENDER (standard reading) -- ROUND 2, RESPONSE

# DEFENDER'S REPLY, ROUND 2: re-seating the loins, the "till", and the registers in their chain

The challenger's points are ammunition. The case is the chain: Luke 1:34-35 and Matthew 1:18-25 fix the conception, Romans 1:3 and Galatians 4:4 fix the flesh, and Matthew 1 and Luke 2 fix the legal name. The challenger must break the chain, not one link.

## 1. The question: "How is it evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda?" (Hebrews 7:14)

**[L1]** Hebrews 7:14: "it is evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda." **[L2]** *Prodēlon* (plainly manifest, publicly known) states that the fact is open. It does not state the route.

**[L1]** The text gives two routes, which the chain keeps apart.

- **The legal route.** Matthew 1:1: "the son of David, the son of Abraham." Matthew 1:16: "Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary." Matthew 1:20-21: "thou son of David… thou shalt call his name JESUS." Matthew 1:24-25: Joseph "took unto him his wife… and he called his name JESUS."
- **The flesh route.** Romans 1:3: "made of the seed of David according to the flesh." Galatians 4:4: "made of a woman."

**[L3]** The law of reckoning separates the registered name from the begetter.

- Deuteronomy 25:5-6: the firstborn "shall succeed in the name of his brother which is dead."
- Genesis 48:5: "thy two sons… are mine; as Reuben and Simeon, they shall be mine."
- Exodus 2:10: "he became her son. And she called his name Moses."
- Esther 2:7: Mordecai "took her for his own daughter."

In each case the register and the begetter are different persons. Naming and taking are acts of legal sonship, and Matthew 1:21 and 1:25 give those acts to Joseph.

**[L3]** Numbers 1:2 and 1:18 (the father's house) are rules of a census of males "by their polls." They do not state that tribal standing never passed through a woman.

- Numbers 32:41 calls Jair "the son of Manasseh," and 1 Chronicles 2:21-22 gives his line through Hezron and "the daughter of Machir."
- 1 Chronicles 2:34-35: Sheshan "had no sons, but daughters," and gave his daughter to his servant, and her line is reckoned.
- Ezra 2:61: the priest "took a wife of the daughters of Barzillai… and was called after their name." Here a wife's house gave the name.

**[L4]** Footing: [L1] Matthew 1:20-25 and Hebrews 7:14, and [L3] Deuteronomy 25:5-6, Exodus 2:10, Numbers 32:41 with 1 Chronicles 2:21-22. The chain: the text has a legal route (Joseph names and takes) and a flesh route (Romans 1:3 with Galatians 4:4), and its own examples show the register following the legal father or the wife's house. So Hebrews 7:14 does not require Joseph's loins. It requires only that the registered line be open, and Matthew 1 opens it.

Noted: no KJV verse names Mary's father. Not conceding here. Goes to review. The chain does not need that name, as §2 shows.

## 2. "Loins" and "bowels" (Acts 2:30; 2 Samuel 7:12): the idiom is descent at any depth

**[L1]** Genesis 46:26: "All the souls that came with Jacob into Egypt, **which came out of his loins**, besides Jacob's sons' wives." This covers grandsons. **[L1]** Hebrews 7:10: Levi "was yet in the loins of his father [Abraham], when Melchisedec met him." Levi was Abraham's great-grandson.

**[L2]** *Osphys* (loins) at Acts 2:30 is the word the challenger himself cites from Hebrews 7:9-10. The challenger's own witness therefore shows that "loins" reaches through several generations, and through mothers' wombs as well, since Levi was born of Leah and Jochebed.
